name: Schizachyrium

project_scope.note: The current project pool has one canonical Schizachyrium anchor; species taxonomy/range decisions remain in the species package.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Start with the whole architecture: a tight bunch with an upper culm that branches into many short terminal fuzzy racemes. At seed, those small racemes turn silvery and fluffy rather than forming one large fingerlike head.
priority: short terminal fuzzy racemes on branchlets

comparisons.rule: Schizachyrium scatters many short racemes across branched upper stems; Bothriochloa concentrates its rames into a more unified terminal head whose node hair and branch architecture are major ID clues.
Anatherum glomeratum builds a dense brushlike fluffy crown; Schizachyrium scoparium shows repeated short racemes terminating separate upper branchlets.

visual_needs: annotated whole-plant image tracing the branched upper culm and its short terminal racemes
side-by-side with KR bluestem showing distributed short racemes versus a compact fingerlike terminal head
